title: Efficient Serving Operating Model — experiment playbook for batching, caching, quantization
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Objective: Create a repeatable operating model and field-playbook for running high-confidence cost-savings experiments across hosted, dedicated and private deployments. The playbook will standardize hypothesis formulation, traffic gating, quality/regression detection, and rollout criteria for batching, KV-cache tuning (TTL/segmentation) and aggressive quantization profiles.

Scope: Pilot matrix will include: 1) dynamic batching profiles (30/60/120ms windows), 2) KV cache TTL adjustments and prefix-aware invalidation, 3) 4-bit/8-bit quantized model variants with calibration. Experiments will target conversational and single-shot generation workloads that represent >60% of RD usage.

Success hypothesis: We can reduce token-level cost by >=18% on average for targeted workloads with <=1.5% relative quality regression (per evaluation suite) and P95 latency impact <20ms for latency-sensitive tiers.

Stakeholders: PMs (Aisha Kumar, Marcus Lee), Eng (Serving runtime: Markus Chen, Infra: Priya Patel), Research/ML (Dr. Elena Soto), DX (Samir Rao), Solutions Eng (Evie Park).
acceptance_criteria: A/B experiment framework instrumented end-to-end with feature flags and rollout controls for hosted + dedicated clusters
Clear experiment matrix (workload, batch window, TTL, quant profile) and a gating dashboard with cost / quality / latency panels
At least 3 field pilots run across representative customers/internal tenants with annotated quality checks and customer-facing rollback plan
Automated alerting for quality regressions tied to evaluation prompt sets and explicit thresholds
Runbook for converting a successful pilot into a staged rollout (canary -> ramp -> full) with safety nets
updates: 2026-02-28: Kickoff — aligned on objectives with ENG/Research/DX. Drafted experiment hypothesis and target metrics. Assigned ENG owners for SDK flags and telemetry schema (ENG-7812).
2026-03-03: Design review — DX proposed dashboard panels and suggested adding per-route token breakup; accepted with minor changes. Ref: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-designs/serving-prism

2026-03-05: Eng spike complete — basic batching window control and KV TTL knobs implemented on a feature branch. Perf microbenchmarks show 10–12% cost improvement on synthetic conversational traces for 60ms window. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3387

2026-03-07: Trade-off discussion — Research warns about hallucination delta for aggressive 4-bit quant on certain decoders; decided to restrict initial quant pilots to reranking and embeddings tasks. Follow-up: create specialized eval sets (ELENA-quant-suite).

2026-03-10: Safety gates defined — added automatic rollback when evaluation regression >1.5% OR customer complaint volume >2x baseline in 1 hour window. Ops runbook draft uploaded. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SE/Serving+Efficiency+Playbook
